title: Finite and completed coefficient pullback unit coordinates and quotient projections
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite coefficient extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, finite quotient coefficient sheaves $B_{W,m}$ of exponent $m+1$, and the completed coefficient sheaf $R_W$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. For every morphism $f:X\to Y$ of schemes [def-pc-scheme], intrinsic finite pullback multiplication on the regular coefficient module [def-sp-finite-intrinsic-pullback, def-sp-finite-intrinsic-direct-adjunction] is invertible; applying the exact single-complex comparison gives the finite derived coefficient-unit isomorphism [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-constant-weil-structure, def-sf-finite-rational-derived-operations, def-weil-constant-coefficient-objects]. There exists a unique strict integral chain unit into the specified Roos pullback complex whose every finite generator is the adjunction image of one and whose shifted cone component is zero [def-pur-integral-finite-pullback, def-pur-integral-operation-complex-models]. Its localization is invertible, giving the completed derived coefficient-unit isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-trf-integral-pullback-descent-model]. Finite multiplication commutes with the actual quotient transitions. The strict integral unit sends every regular section a, under the mth unshifted Roos projection, to its actual quotient coefficient times the normalized finite generator. For an isomorphism f, these finite and integral unit identifications equal the recorded canonical Weil identifications [lem-pod-canonical-coefficient-pullback-reduction, def-zl-finite-regular-coefficient-comparisons].

proof.text: The finite intrinsic multiplication is the adjoint of the constant regular section one. Transposing it computes its value on every adjunction generator. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies it with the usual ringed-site regular-module multiplication. The base-change functor preserves the terminal object and hence is final, so the regular-module multiplication is an isomorphism. The exact single-complex comparison gives its finite derived isomorphism.

Apply the proved normalizedChainUnit_isIso theorem to this unique chain map, and compose its inverse with the specified integral derived-pullback comparison.

proof.text: For isomorphisms, the proved coefficientFiniteKappa_formula identifies the canonical finite comparison with the inverse-image regular comparison followed by inverse pulled regular comparison. The two intrinsic multiplication maps have the same adjoint and therefore coincide. Taking degree zero proves finiteUnit_canonicalWeil. The integral comparison follows by canceling the inverse comparison isomorphisms and the uniqueness of the normalized strict unit.

proof.text: Naturality of sheafification in the quotient ring map and the generator computation prove the actual finite quotient square. For an arbitrary regular section a, linearity of the strict integral unit identifies its image with a times its image on one. The normalization computes that latter image; the target scalar action factors through the actual quotient projection. This proves integralUnit_projection for every section, not merely the generator.

theorem integralUnit_projection {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (m : ℕ) (V : Y.ProEt)
    (a : (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l E X).obj.obj
      (op ((proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V))) :
    ((integralChainUnit l E f).f 0 ≫
      (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.fst
        (constantWeilPullbackRoosEndomorphism l E f)).f 0 ≫
      (Pi.π (fun j ↦ (constantWeilPullbackTower l E f).obj (op j)) m).f 0).val.app
        (op ((proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V))
      (((HomologicalComplex.singleObjXSelf (.up ℤ) 0
        (SheafOfModules.unit (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l E X))).inv.val.app
          (op ((proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V))) a) =
      @SMul.smul
        ((integralCoefficientSheaf l E X m).obj.obj
          (op ((proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V)))
        (((integralOperationsLevelPullback l E f m).obj
          (((unrestrictedIntegralFiniteComplex l E Y m).obj
            (constantWeilIntegralComplex l E Y)).X 0)).val.obj
              (op ((proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V))) inferInstance
        ((limit.π (integralCoefficientSheafSystem l E X) (op m)).hom.app
          (op ((proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V)) a)
          (integralOperationsPullbackGenerator l E f m
            (((unrestrictedIntegralFiniteComplex l E Y m).obj
              (constantWeilIntegralComplex l E Y)).X 0) V
            (constantWeilReducedUnitSection l E Y m V))
